title: A Preregistered, Artifact‑Backed Paired Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Pipeline for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a fully reproducible paired experiment (GVR‑ProtocolEval‑2026‑PR1) to compare LLM‑only configuration generation and a guarded generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline on 200 stratified intent→configuration NetOps tasks in a Dockerized Mininet emulator with a deterministic validator. Under the frozen plan we generated a single shared LLM candidate per task (generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate") and evaluated that same candidate under both arms. All confirmatory episodes were verifier‑accepted: baseline 200/200, guarded 200/200 (n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); McNemar exact p = 1.0. We release the full preregistration (SHA‑256 d913b4167cc6aa85b283e0703e0bfff0c3e8864405f5159d9a1a1cf5fc3fafdc), execution manifest and raw artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 d76af611272bd8e8b3a94290efecd6ecf634c5f3e36c2450c4245985e96931fb), representative validator traces (e.g. execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 9235bce7875c1717dff5ac6be49c5769929b4e8509f5df404127efe9d6ee938f), and analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c). The observed null is a reproducible boundary condition of the preregistered shared‑candidate semantics (no repairs were applied in confirmatory episodes); we therefore document artifact‑grounded diagnostics, the exact provenance of every principal number, and a minimal, artifact‑supported road map for the preregistered follow‑ups needed to evaluate active repair.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation is operationally valuable but safety‑critical: incorrect device changes can cause reachability loss, policy violation, or outages. Generate→validate→repair (GVR) pipelines pair LLM generation with deterministic validators and bounded repair loops to improve operational trustworthiness. Prior benchmarks (NetConfEval, OpsEval, NetEval) explore translation performance and LLM capability; however, few studies publish a fully preregistered, artifact‑archived, deterministic paired test that freezes both generation and scoring semantics. We preregistered, executed, and archived such a run (GVR‑ProtocolEval‑2026‑PR1) and publish the complete artifact bundle so every principal number is traceable to immutable files. The preregistered research question asked whether a guarded GVR pipeline reduces operational‑failure rates (reachability loss or policy violation) relative to LLM‑only generation in a paired within‑task design under controlled Mininet emulation and fault injection.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps and AIOps includes NetConfEval (intent→configuration benchmarks) and OpsEval/NetEval (AIOps/NetOps task suites and multi‑model evaluations). Generate‑validate‑repair ideas echo learning‑based program repair and guarded execution in safety engineering. We position our contribution as a reproducibility‑focused, preregistered paired design with deterministic validator traces and full artifact hashes, extending prior evaluation work by publishing the run manifest and validator outputs so the exact experiment can be replayed and analyzed (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and freeze. We preregistered a detailed machine‑readable plan (GVR‑ProtocolEval‑2026‑PR1) that froze: (1) primary estimand (paired difference in binary operational‑failure indicator), (2) confirmatory design (200 tasks stratified across five protocol groups × two modalities), (3) inference plan (bootstrap 10,000 resamples, seed=1729; exact McNemar test), (4) model (gpt‑5‑mini; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), (5) generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (single LLM draw per task reused under both baseline and guarded arms), (6) validator id deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and scoring rules, (7) contamination check (token overlap ≥80% triggers exclusion), and (8) bounded retry policy limited to infrastructure recovery. The preregistration SHA‑256 is d913b4167cc6aa85b283e0703e0bfff0c3e8864405f5159d9a1a1cf5fc3fafdc (archived). Task bank and emulator. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced a confirmatory bank of 200 intent→configuration tasks (approx. 20 tasks per protocol×modality cluster) and a 50‑task exploratory set; task manifests and hashes are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 c1bd4a09...). Each task encodes initial state, final expected state, explicit safety constraints (allowed fields and workflow policies), and a solvable template. Execution harness. For each task we executed a single shared LLM candidate (shared_initial) and then applied the deterministic validator under the two scoring conditions (baseline vs guarded) without altering the candidate. All provider calls, raw responses, validator logs, scoring JSONs, and the full execution manifest were archived and hashed (execution/execution_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 d76af611...). Scoring and statistical plan. The primary analysis is the paired mean difference in the binary operational‑failure indicator, estimated by bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and tested with exact McNemar. Contamination and exclusions. Automated token‑overlap checks versus a curated vendor/RFC corpus were preregistered; items with ≥80% overlap would be excluded. Deterministic reproducibility. All artifacts (prompts, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, analysis scripts) are archived with SHA‑256 hashes so the entire pipeline can be deterministically reproduced; representative artifact paths and SHA‑256 values are cited in the Disclosure Statement and Results.
sections.results: Execution summary. Planned episodes = 400 (200 tasks × 2 arms); completed episodes = 400; failed episodes = 0. Model calls used = 200 (one shared-generation per task as preregistered). All raw artifacts and hashes are archived (execution/execution_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 d76af611272bd8e8b3a94290efecd6ecf634c5f3e36c2450c4245985e96931fb). Confirmatory outcomes. Scoring summary (analysis artifacts): baseline verifier‑accepted = 200/200; guarded verifier‑accepted = 200/200. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a4...) is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Primary inferential outputs: paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative scorings. Representative archived scoring JSONs contain the validator trace and final_state snapshot (examples with archived SHA‑256s): execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 9235bce7...), execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json (SHA‑256 25e2c0c7...), execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json (SHA‑256 20e953b1...). Each scoring JSON shows parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validator verdict, and normalized_configuration—permitting precise inspection of what checks passed. Artifact‑grounded diagnostic analysis. Because the preregistered semantics used a single shared LLM candidate per task, repair_applied=false across confirmatory episodes; hence no repair loop was exercised. To explain baseline=100% we inspected artifacts: (A) contamination_summary.csv (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0...) recorded zero confirmatory flags under the preregistered ≥80% token overlap rule, so no tasks were excluded for overt token duplication; (B) validator traces archived in each scoring JSON enumerate the rule classes exercised and show that for the synthetic templates the generated candidate matched the validator's required sequences (e.g., validation_after.required_command_count equals parsed_command_count and valid=true in the representative JSONs); (C) task manifests show tasks were constructed from solvable templates explicitly intended to be satisfied by straightforward command sequences (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 c1bd4a09...). These artifact‑grounded observations explain the observed 100% acceptance under the executed boundary condition without inventing training‑data overlap claims. Reproducibility artifacts. The full artifact bundle (preregistration, model configuration, provider traces, raw responses, validator scoring JSONs, analysis scripts and outputs) is archived with SHA‑256 manifests; principal artifact hashes are included in the Disclosure Statement and in the Results paragraph above.
sections.discussion: Interpretation of the confirmatory null. The preregistered paired contrast compared the same generated candidate under both arms; therefore the run measured whether the deterministic validator accepted that candidate, not whether active repairs would have changed the outcome. Observing baseline=100% acceptance is thus a valid, reproducible boundary‑condition outcome of the preregistered semantics but does not adjudicate whether an actively applied GVR repair loop would improve operational safety in harder or production settings. Artifact‑grounded reasons for 100% acceptance. The archived evidence supports the following nonexclusive causes: (1) validator rule scope and the chosen checks (parsing/presence checks and a small set of dependency rules) matched the solvable synthetic templates—scoring JSONs show required_command_count equals parsed_command_count and valid=true for representative tasks; (2) the task generator produced solvable vendor‑like templates by construction (task manifests archived); (3) the single shared LLM draw was sufficient to produce the required sequences for the sampled templates. Limits of inference and power. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline failure rate and targeted an absolute 10 percentage‑point paired reduction with 80% power; observed baseline success=100% violates that assumption, rendering the original MDE plan inapplicable. We therefore report exact counts and the artifact‑backed paired table rather than claiming achieved power. Operational implications. The study demonstrates the practical value of preregistration plus full artifact archiving: when a confirmatory run produces an unexpected boundary outcome, the complete artifact set allows deterministic forensic diagnosis (validator logs, task manifests, provider traces, contamination scans, and hashes). This enables immediate, reproducible follow‑ups without guessing. Recommended artifact‑supported follow‑ups (deterministic and preregisterable). All follow‑ups listed below are feasible using the archived code and manifests (no new data fabrication): (A) Reexecute a revised preregistered run with independent_generation_per_arm=true so baseline and guarded arms receive independent LLM draws and repairs can be applied; (B) expand validator coverage to include timing‑sensitive checks and active reachability probes (the deterministic validator code and scoring harness are archived and can be extended reproducibly); (C) increase adversariality by adding template variants that break simple required‑command checks (task generator parameters are archived and can be modified deterministically). Each follow‑up should be preregistered and archived with deterministic hashes to preserve the reproducibility discipline demonstrated here.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a fully artifacted paired experiment comparing LLM‑only generation and a guarded GVR pipeline on 200 synthetic intent→configuration tasks. Under the frozen shared‑candidate semantics no repair activity occurred and both arms were verifier‑accepted on all tasks (n11=200), producing a paired difference of 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00], McNemar p=1.0). This outcome is a reproducible boundary condition caused by the preregistered generation semantics and the solvable synthetic task templates—documented by the archived scoring JSONs and contamination scans. We publish the full preregistration, execution manifest, raw model outputs, validator traces, contamination scans, and analysis artifacts (SHA‑256s given above) so the run can be deterministically replayed and the minimal preregistered follow‑ups (independent draws per arm; expanded validator coverage) can be executed to evaluate active repair efficacy. The principal scientific contribution is methodological: we demonstrate how strict preregistration plus complete artifact archival and deterministic validator traces can convert an unexpected null into a precisely diagnosable, reproducible boundary result and provide the exact inputs needed for a tightly constrained, artifact‑backed next experiment that tests the originally intended scientific contrast. We therefore recommend that future NetOps GVR evaluations (and AIOps benchmarks) adopt the same preregistration + full‑artifact publication discipline to make claims auditable and reproducible at the command and validator trace level.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track).
- LLM(s) used: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820).
- Orchestration/adapter framework: hosted_netops_gvr_v1.
- Exact initial master prompt immutable archived reference (required): provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.
- Research Director role: the human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved preregistration constraints before the autonomy lock; after the lock the autonomous system performed literature review, study selection, preregistration creation, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting without human technical editing of numbers, validator outputs, or manuscript technical content.
- Preregistration/frozen plan: GVR‑ProtocolEval‑2026‑PR1 (SHA‑256 d913b4167cc6aa85b283e0703e0bfff0c3e8864405f5159d9a1a1cf5fc3fafdc). The preregistered design froze generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (single LLM candidate per task evaluated under both arms), primary estimand, bootstrap parameters (10,000 resamples, seed=1729), contingency power plan, contamination checks, and bounded retry policy.
- Tools and experiment generation: deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), Dockerized Mininet emulator; all manifests and code used in the run are archived and hashed (execution/execution_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 d76af611272bd8e8b3a94290efecd6ecf634c5f3e36c2450c4245985e96931fb).
- Provider traces and raw outputs: all provider calls and raw responses were archived; representative provider traces are at execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json (SHA‑256 bb0602268dcd1fe12d6ddd5c4a9afcc3a0141a03dc8bd4355d76be5c7a9aa7c6) and a complete call cache is available in execution/call_cache/ (many SHA‑256 entries archived in the execution manifest).
- Preregistered contamination policy and checks: token overlap ≥80% triggers exclusion; contamination scan results are archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). No confirmatory tasks were excluded under the preregistered rule.
- Autonomous analysis and statistics: paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and exact McNemar test were preregistered and executed deterministically; primary outputs are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c, analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951).
- Autonomous peer review and revision: the system ran an autonomous internal review and incorporated reviewer‑required clarifications that could be supported by archived artifacts (e.g., inclusion of representative scoring JSON hashes). No human edited the technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock.
- Technical restarts: only preregistered retries for infrastructure recovery were performed; no reruns were used to alter scientific outcomes. All execution logs and retry records are archived (execution/execution_log.jsonl SHA‑256 a5659f3ac8ca4cf9a6b9dadaab1752af9dcebc4e7c370f0a93a234586cb55873).
- Pre‑lock development: collaborative infrastructure and generator/validator rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were not used as evidence; all empirical results reported here derive from the post‑lock frozen run and its archived artifacts.
- Reproducibility: the full artifact bundle (preregistration, model configuration, provider traces, raw responses, validator scoring JSONs, analysis scripts and outputs) is archived with SHA‑256 manifests and paths cited above so the exact run can be deterministically reproduced by independent auditors.
limitations: Emulation and scope: the confirmatory bank used synthetic vendor‑like templates and a Dockerized Mininet emulator; production hardware/firmware heterogeneity and timing side effects are not represented.

Shared‑candidate design: the preregistered generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate" produced one LLM draw per task reused in both arms; as a consequence no repair loop was exercised in confirmatory episodes, so the run does not test active repair efficacy.

Validator construct coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applies a finite set of syntactic and dependency checks; broader operational properties (complex timing, firmware side effects, or richer policy reasoning) lie outside this validator's covered construct.

Power‑plan mismatch: the preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline failure rate and targeted a 10 percentage‑point paired reduction; observed baseline success=100% invalidates that assumption and prevents claiming the planned MDE was tested.
Contamination detection limits: token‑overlap scans flagged no confirmatory exclusions under the preregistered threshold, but nondiscoverable pretraining overlap cannot be fully excluded.
External generalizability: the outcome under the executed boundary semantics does not generalize to other models, per‑arm sampling regimes, stronger validators, or production device fleets.
